create.title: Exact post-collar smoothing and far height-alias reduction
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), y=floor(sqrt X), N=floor X=y^2+q with 0<=q<=2y, and fix 0<rho_1<rho_2<1/8. Put L_(i,h)=floor(rho_i y/sqrt(h)), D_(i,h)=y-L_(i,h)-1, and let r_(2,h) be the least positive odd integer at least 4Nh/D_(2,h)^2 on every nonempty row. The literal sharp Round-139 tail S_(N,rho_1)^pm is target-equivalent to the clean far stationary scalar P_(rho_2)^+=e(-1/8)N^(1/4) sum_h sum_(r>=r_(2,h)+2, r odd) chi_4(r)(hr)^(-3/4)V_low(R^2hr/N)e(sqrt(Nhr)), with the negative scalar its conjugate: S_(N,rho_1)^pm=P_(rho_2)^pm+O(R log^C(2X)) for a fixed C. The proof first smooths only across L_(1,h)<y-d<=L_(2,h), costing O(R log X) by the accepted exact-curvature collar; the smooth amplitude has flat endpoints and norms ||A||_infinity+||A'||_1<<h^(-1), ||A''||_1<<h^(-1)((Rh)^(-1)+Delta_h^(-1)). A rowwise smooth B-process, with the cutoff derivative localized to O(sqrt(h)) ramp aliases and remote aliases integrated twice, has error O(h^(-1)log^2(2X)); the height sum is O(log^3(2X)). The full ramp and r_(2,h) cost O(R log X), and r>=r_(2,h)+2 is many Gaussian widths inside the plateau. Thus the first open estimate is |P_(rho_2)^pm|<<_epsilon R X^epsilon. This is an unsquared scalar equivalence only; no residual sub-square or collar-tail cross term is removed.
create.next_action: Prove the X^epsilon bound for the exact grouped far sum sum_m m^(-3/4)V_low(R^2m/N)A_(rho_2)(m)e(sqrt(Nm)), using signed control of near-radical and nonsquare incomplete product fibres. Do not replace A_(rho_2) by the complete r_2(m)/4 fibre or square the scalar reduction.

create.title: Sharp endpoint, rank-one height-alias, and incomplete product-fibre obstruction
create.statement_tex: For the literal sharp post-collar tail, each nonzero endpoint row has dual asymptotic I_(h,r)^sharp=A_h(D_h)e(Nh/D_h+rD_h/4)/(2 pi i(r/4-Nh/D_h^2))+O_h(r^(-2)); hence the raw odd-alias family is not absolutely separable and its half-endpoint plus branchwise principal-value order are essential. After the proved two-collar smoothing, the clean survivor groups exactly as P=e(-1/8)N^(1/4) sum_(m<<y)m^(-3/4)V_low(R^2m/N)A_(rho_2)(m)e(sqrt(Nm)), where A_(rho_2)(m)=sum_(h|m, r=m/h odd, r>=r_(2,h)+2)chi_4(r). The joint phase sqrt(Nhr) has Hessian determinant zero and rank one, also after r=4h+s. Coefficient-blind modulus has matching R^(3/2+o(1)) capacity, witnessed on the h=1 plateau. The incomplete mask does not force character cancellation: for sufficiently large odd fourth-power centres and supported m=p^(2a), p=1 mod 4, A_(rho_2)(p^(2a))=a. If N=Du^2 with D squarefree, the exact radical channel m=Dt^2 has absolute mass O_epsilon(RD^(-3/4)X^epsilon), but near radicals and nonsquare incomplete fibres remain open. A second Legendre step returns the reciprocal phase N/z and completing the fibre returns r_2(m)/4. These are scoped no-go controls, not a target failure or a signed lower bound.
create.next_action: Park sharp aliaswise modulus, closest-alias deletion, generic nondegenerate two-variable Hessian estimates, complete-fibre replacement, exact-radical extrapolation, and another formal Legendre transform. Reopen only with an actual signed theorem for the incomplete coefficient over near-radical and nonsquare phases.

update.next_action: The exact sharp post-collar tail is now target-equivalent to the clean far product-fibre scalar P_(rho_2). Prove its grouped weighted sum at X^epsilon through signed near-radical and nonsquare incomplete-fibre cancellation; retain the scalar-only direction and the open Round-138 cross term.

The literal complement of the exact curvature collar is now reduced, after a second target-safe collar band, to the clean far alias scalar P_(rho_2). Prove the X^epsilon grouped incomplete-fibre sum; do not infer a tail-square identity.

The former nonprincipal-owner caveat is now resolved after a lawful two-collar smoothing: all discarded owners are target-safe and the exact far scalar remains. Retain the sharp principal-value warning, rank-one product geometry, and exact-radical bound; reopen only through signed near-radical and nonsquare incomplete-fibre control.

reject.reason: Every nonzero sharp endpoint row has a harmonic 1/r boundary tail; the half-endpoint and branchwise symmetric ordering are essential.
The closest stationary alias is target-safe, but deleting it does not remove the remote principal-value boundary series.
The sharp formula also contains its half-endpoint, transition, nonstationary, profile-crossing, and conditionally summed boundary owners.
The complete band up to the rho_2 threshold lies in the smoothing ramp; the retained clean bulk starts only at r_(2,h)+2.
Its exact derivative-image interval contains O(1+sqrt(h)) odd aliases, all of which must be priced.
One integration reproduces a harmonic tail; flat endpoints and two integrations are required for absolute summation.
The cutoff derivative must be localized to the O(sqrt(h)) aliases whose stationary neighborhoods meet the smoothing ramp.
The Hessian of sqrt(Nhr) has determinant zero and rank one, invariant under the exact linear change r=4h+s.
The phase is homogeneous of degree one and has a radial null direction; rational rays remain linear.
The height-dependent far mask truncates the divisor fibre; r_2(m)/4 is only the complete-mask comparison.
Supported prime-square fibres with p=1 mod 4 have the exact same-sign value A_(rho_2)(p^(2a))=a.
Coefficient-blind modulus has matching R^(3/2+o(1)) capacity, losing R^(1/2) against the target.
The h=1 plateau controls only the sum of term moduli; cancellation with the rest of the scalar remains possible.
The character-correct ray has only target-scale mass and is not isolated from the rest of the signed scalar.
The proof applies only when Nm is a square; no spacing or cancellation estimate for near-square phases is obtained.
Its critical value is the original reciprocal phase N/z, and completion of the fibre returns the sum-of-two-squares interface.
The collar-tail cross term and the lift-dependent cutoff remain uncontrolled; only unsquared target equivalence is proved.
The far signed estimate, lower GAR, both direct M1 parents, all M2 parents, endpoint uniformity, M9, the bridge, and the target remain open.

no_change.reason: Round 140 sharpens only the alternative lower-radial scalar interface and proves neither complete lower GAR nor both direct blockwise M1 parents.
Hard TOP, BAL, and every required UNBAL owner remain open.
A smoothed reduction for one lower-scalar tail is not an all-owner endpoint-uniformity theorem.
M9-M1, M9-M2, and endpoint uniformity remain open.
The bridge remains conditional on the complete open M9 hypothesis.
The strongest internally proved global exponent remains one third.
The separately audited external exponent remains (3292+25sqrt(1717))/13762.
The quarter target still lacks the far incomplete-fibre scalar bound, the remaining M1 and M2 owners, endpoint uniformity, M9, and an unconditional final bridge.

round_assessment.reason: Round 140 rigorously resolves every endpoint, smoothing, transition, nonstationary, profile, and stationary-remainder owner in the post-collar character-Poisson route and reduces the literal tail to one exact signed far product-fibre scalar. It also identifies sharp principal-value, rank-one, coefficient-blind capacity, incomplete-fibre, near-radical, and self-return barriers without overstating them. The decisive far signed estimate and every downstream exponent remain open.
